source.publication: 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and Form CT-1040
source.section: PDF page 19, Table A (MFS column, more than 29,000 to 30,000: 6,000); PDF page 20, Table B (one schedule for Single or Married Filing Separately); PDF page 23, Table E (MFS, more than 27,000 to 48,000: .10); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 30,000.00 = 30,000.00. Federal taxable income = 30,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction = 14,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 30,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 30,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 0.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 0.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 30,000.00 - 0.00 = 30,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 30,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 30,000.00 is more than 29,000.00, exemption 6,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 30,000.00 - 6,000.00 = 24,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Single or Married Filing Separately schedule) on 24,000.00: 10,000.00 x 0.02 + 14,000.00 x 0.045 = 200.00 + 630.00 = 830.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 30,000.00 is not more than 50,250.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 105,000.00); Line 7 = 830.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.10 (Connecticut AGI 30,000.00 is in the band more than 27,000.00); Line 9 = 830.00 x 0.10 = 83.00. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 830.00 - 83.00 = 747.00 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Married filing separately has its own Table A and Table E columns but uses the single Table B schedule (the projection has no married_separate brackets).
